sanskrit: brahmadatta uvāca yatkṛte pratikuryād vai na sa tatrāparādhnuyāt anṛṇas tena bhavati vasa pūjani mā gamaḥ
english: Brahmadatta said: When one requites a deed by repaying it in kind, in that he commits no offense; thereby he is freed of his debt. Dwell here, Pūjanī; do not depart.

sanskrit: pūjany uvāca na kṛtasya na kartuś ca sakhyaṃ saṃdhīyate punaḥ hṛdayaṃ tatra jānāti kartuś caiva kṛtasya ca
english: Pūjanī said: Between the wrong that was done and the one who did it, friendship is never knit together again; the heart there knows the truth, both of the doer and of the deed.

sanskrit: brahmadatta uvāca kṛtasya caiva kartuś ca sakhyaṃ saṃdhīyate punaḥ vairasyopaśamo dṛṣṭaḥ pāpaṃ nopāśnute punaḥ
english: Brahmadatta said: Between the deed and the one who did it friendship can be knit together again; a quieting of enmity is seen, and one need not again suffer evil.

sanskrit: pūjany uvāca nāsti vairam upakrāntaṃ sāntvito 'smīti nāśvaset viśvāsād badhyate bālas tasmāc chreyo hy adarśanam
english: Pūjanī said: Enmity once begun is not undone. Let no one trust, thinking 'I have been appeased'; the fool is destroyed through his trust. Therefore it is better not to meet at all.

sanskrit: tarasā ye na śakyante śastraiḥ suniśitair api sāmnā te vinigṛhyante gajā iva kareṇubhiḥ
english: Those who cannot be subdued by force, nor even by sharp-honed weapons, are mastered by soft words, as bull-elephants are by cow-elephants.

sanskrit: brahmadatta uvāca saṃvāsāj jāyate sneho jīvitāntakareṣv api anyonyasya ca viśvāsaḥ śvapacena śuno yathā
english: Brahmadatta said: From living together affection arises, even among those who would end one's life, and mutual trust as well, as between the dog and the outcaste dog-cooker.

sanskrit: anyonyakṛtavairāṇāṃ saṃvāsān mṛdutāṃ gatam naiva tiṣṭhati tad vairaṃ puṣkarastham ivodakam
english: Among those who have wronged one another, the enmity, softened by their living together, does not abide, like water resting on a lotus leaf.

sanskrit: pūjany uvāca vairaṃ pañcasamutthānaṃ tac ca budhyanti paṇḍitāḥ strīkṛtaṃ vāstujaṃ vāgjaṃ sasapatnāparādhajam
english: Pūjanī said: Enmity arises from five sources, and the wise understand this: that caused by a woman, that born of property, that born of speech, and that born of a rival's offense.

sanskrit: tatra dātā nihantavyaḥ kṣatriyeṇa viśeṣataḥ prakāśaṃ vāprakāśaṃ vā buddhvā deśabalādikam
english: In such a case the one who inflicts the injury must be slain, especially by a kṣatriya, whether openly or in secret, after weighing place, strength, and the rest.

sanskrit: kṛtavaire na viśvāsaḥ kāryas tv iha suhṛdy api channaṃ saṃtiṣṭhate vairaṃ gūḍho 'gnir iva dāruṣu
english: When enmity has been incurred, no trust should be placed even in one who seems a friend; the enmity persists concealed, like fire hidden within wood.

sanskrit: na vittena na pāruṣyair na sāntvena na ca śrutaiḥ vairāgniḥ śāmyate rājann aurvāgnir iva sāgare
english: Not by wealth, not by harsh measures, not by soothing words, nor by learning is the fire of enmity quenched, O king, any more than the Aurva-fire is quenched in the ocean.

sanskrit: na hi vairāgnir udbhūtaḥ karma vāpy aparādhajam śāmyaty adagdhvā nṛpate vinā hy ekatarakṣayāt
english: For the kindled fire of enmity, or a deed born of offense, does not subside, O lord of men, without burning out one side or the other; only by the destruction of one party does it cease.

sanskrit: satkṛtasyārthamānābhyāṃ syāt tu pūrvāpakāriṇaḥ naiva śāntir na viśvāsaḥ karma trāsayate balāt
english: Even toward one honored with gifts and respect, if he was the first to do harm, there is no real peace and no trust; the remembered deed itself drives one to fear by its force.

sanskrit: naivāpakāre kasmiṃś cid ahaṃ tvayi tathā bhavān viśvāsād uṣitā pūrvaṃ nedānīṃ viśvasāmy aham
english: In no injury have I been at fault toward you, nor you toward me; through trust I dwelt here before, but now I trust no longer.

sanskrit: brahmadatta uvāca kālena kriyate kāryaṃ tathaiva vividhāḥ kriyāḥ kālenaiva pravartante kaḥ kasyehāparādhyati
english: Brahmadatta said: It is by Time that every act is wrought, and likewise the manifold deeds; by Time alone do they come to pass. Who here truly offends against whom?

sanskrit: tulyaṃ cobhe pravartete maraṇaṃ janma caiva ha kāryate caiva kālena tannimittaṃ hi jīvati
english: Both alike come to pass, death and birth as well; both are brought about by Time, and on that ground each creature lives.

sanskrit: badhyante yugapat ke cid ekaikasya na cāpare kālo dahati bhūtāni saṃprāpyāgnir ivendhanam
english: Some are slain all at once, while others, one by one, are not; Time consumes living beings as fire consumes the fuel it reaches.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ pramāṇaṃ naiva tvam anyonyakaraṇe śubhe kālo nityam upādhatte sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca dehinām
english: Neither I nor you are the true cause in the doings, good or ill, that pass between us; it is Time that forever apportions to embodied beings their joy and their sorrow.

sanskrit: evaṃ vaseha sasnehā yathākālam ahiṃsitā yat kṛtaṃ tac ca me kṣāntaṃ tvaṃ caiva kṣama pūjani
english: So dwell here in affection, unharmed as long as Time allows; what was done I have forgiven; do you too forgive, Pūjanī.

sanskrit: pūjany uvāca yadi kālaḥ pramāṇaṃ te na vairaṃ kasya cid bhavet kasmāt tv apacitiṃ yānti bāndhavā bāndhave hate
english: Pūjanī said: If Time is your sole authority, then no one would harbor enmity at all; why then do kinsmen seek to avenge a kinsman when he is slain?

sanskrit: kasmād devāsurāḥ pūrvam anyonyam abhijaghnire yadi kālena niryāṇaṃ sukhaduḥkhe bhavābhavau
english: Why did the gods and the demons of old strike down one another, if it is by Time that release comes, and joy and sorrow, existence and non-existence?

sanskrit: bhiṣajo bheṣajaṃ kartuṃ kasmād icchanti rogiṇe yadi kālena pacyante bheṣajaiḥ kiṃ prayojanam
english: Why do physicians wish to prepare medicine for the sick, if men are ripened by Time alone? What use, then, are remedies?

sanskrit: pralāpaḥ kriyate kasmāt sumahāñ śokamūrchitaiḥ yadi kālaḥ pramāṇaṃ te kasmād dharmo 'sti kartṛṣu
english: Why is loud lamentation made by those stunned with grief, if Time is your sole authority? And why is there any merit attaching to those who act?

sanskrit: tava putro mamāpatyaṃ hatavān hiṃsito mayā anantaraṃ tvayā cāhaṃ bandhanīyā mahīpate
english: Your son slew my offspring, and he was killed by me in turn; thereafter I should rightly have been seized and bound by you, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi putraśokena kṛtapāpā tavātmaje tathā tvayā prahartavyaṃ mayi tattvaṃ ca me śṛṇu
english: For I, in grief for my young, committed an evil deed against your son; therefore you ought to strike at me. Hear now the truth I tell.

sanskrit: bhakṣārthaṃ krīḍanārthaṃ vā narā vāñchanti pakṣiṇaḥ tṛtīyo nāsti saṃyogo vadhabandhād ṛte kṣamaḥ
english: Men desire birds either for food or for sport; no third relation is possible save killing or caging. Be patient and consider this.

sanskrit: vadhabandhabhayād eke mokṣatantram upāgatāḥ maraṇotpātajaṃ duḥkham āhur dharmavido janāḥ
english: Some, from fear of being killed or caged, have taken up the discipline of release; those who know dharma call the suffering born of death and calamity a grievous thing.

sanskrit: sarvasya dayitāḥ prāṇāḥ sarvasya dayitāḥ sutāḥ duḥkhād udvijate sarvaḥ sarvasya sukham īpsitam
english: Dear to every being is its own life; dear to every being are its young. Everyone shrinks from sorrow; happiness is what everyone craves.

sanskrit: duḥkhaṃ jarā brahmadatta duḥkham arthaviparyayaḥ duḥkhaṃ cāniṣṭasaṃvāso duḥkham iṣṭaviyogajam
english: Old age is sorrow, Brahmadatta; the loss of one's wealth is sorrow; sorrow is dwelling with what one dislikes, and sorrow is the parting from what one loves.

sanskrit: vairabandhakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ hiṃsājaṃ strīkṛtaṃ tathā duḥkhaṃ sukhena satataṃ janād viparivartate
english: Sorrow arises from enmity and bondage, from violence, and likewise from a woman; sorrow alternates ceaselessly with joy, turning about from person to person.

sanskrit: na duḥkhaṃ paraduḥkhe vai ke cid āhur abuddhayaḥ yo duḥkhaṃ nābhijānāti sa jalpati mahājane
english: Some unwise men declare that another's sorrow is no real sorrow; but it is he who has not himself known sorrow who prattles so before a crowd.

sanskrit: yas tu śocati duḥkhārtaḥ sa kathaṃ vaktum utsahet rasajñaḥ sarvaduḥkhasya yathātmani tathā pare
english: But one who grieves, afflicted by sorrow, how could he dare to speak so? He who has tasted all sorrow feels it in another as he feels it in himself.

sanskrit: yat kṛtaṃ te mayā rājaṃs tvayā ca mama yat kṛtam na tad varṣaśataiḥ śakyaṃ vyapohitum ariṃdama
english: What I have done to you, O king, and what you have done to me, that cannot be wiped away even in a hundred years, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: āvayoḥ kṛtam anyonyaṃ tatra saṃdhir na vidyate smṛtvā smṛtvā hi te putraṃ navaṃ vairaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: In what we two have done to each other no reconciliation is possible; for as you remember your son again and again, the enmity will arise anew.

sanskrit: vairam antikam āsajya yaḥ prītiṃ kartum icchati mṛnmayasyeva bhagnasya tasya saṃdhir na vidyate
english: He who, with enmity close at hand, wishes to make peace, can no more reunite it than the pieces of a shattered earthen pot.

sanskrit: niścitaś cārthaśāstrajñair aviśvāsaḥ sukhodayaḥ uśanāś cātha gāthe dve prahrādāyābravīt purā
english: Distrust, declared by those versed in the science of statecraft, yields happiness; and long ago Uśanas spoke two verses to Prahrāda.

sanskrit: ye vairiṇaḥ śraddadhate satye satyetare 'pi vā te śraddadhānā vadhyante madhu śuṣkatṛṇair yathā
english: Those who, being enemies, place their faith in a foe, whether he is truthful or untruthful, are destroyed by their trusting, as one might be by honey set among dry grass.

sanskrit: na hi vairāṇi śāmyanti kuleṣv ā daśamād yugāt ākhyātāraś ca vidyante kule ced vidyate pumān
english: For enmities are not quenched in families even to the tenth generation; and there will always be those to recount them, so long as a single man of the line survives.

sanskrit: upaguhya hi vairāṇi sāntvayanti narādhipāḥ athainaṃ pratipiṃṣanti pūrṇaṃ ghaṭam ivāśmani
english: Kings, concealing their enmities, speak soothingly; then they crush their foe, as one dashes a brimming pot upon a stone.

sanskrit: sadā na viśvased rājan pāpaṃ kṛtveha kasya cit apakṛtya pareṣāṃ hi viśvāsād duḥkham aśnute
english: Never should one trust, O king, after having wrought evil against anyone here; for having injured others, one reaps sorrow through misplaced trust.

sanskrit: brahmadatta uvāca nāviśvāsāc cinvate 'rthān nehante cāpi kiṃ cana bhayād ekatarān nityaṃ mṛtakalpā bhavanti ca
english: Brahmadatta said: Through distrust men gather no wealth, nor do they strive for anything; ever in fear of one side or another, they become as good as dead.

sanskrit: pūjany uvāca yasyeha vraṇinau pādau padbhyāṃ ca parisarpati kṣaṇyete tasya tau pādau suguptam abhidhāvataḥ
english: Pūjanī said: He whose two feet here are wounded, yet who goes about upon them, sees those very feet worn raw, even though he treads with utmost care.

sanskrit: netrābhyāṃ sarujābhyāṃ yaḥ prativātam udīkṣate tasya vāyurujātyarthaṃ netrayor bhavati dhruvam
english: He who, with eyes already aching, looks straight into the wind, surely suffers a yet sharper pain from the wind within his eyes.

sanskrit: duṣṭaṃ panthānam āśritya yo mohād abhipadyate ātmano balam ajñātvā tad antaṃ tasya jīvitam
english: He who in his delusion takes to a perilous road, not knowing his own strength, finds in that the end of his life.

sanskrit: yas tu varṣam avijñāya kṣetraṃ kṛṣati mānavaḥ hīnaṃ puruṣakāreṇa sasyaṃ naivāpnute punaḥ
english: The man who plows his field without regard to the rains, falling short in human effort, never wins his harvest.

sanskrit: yaś ca tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ vāpy āsvādavidhuraṃ hitam āhāraṃ kurute nityaṃ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate
english: And he who takes wholesome food, though it be bitter or astringent and unpleasant to the taste, makes himself fit for long life and well-being.

sanskrit: pathyaṃ bhuktvā naro lobhād yo 'nyad aśnāti bhojanam pariṇāmam avijñāya tad antaṃ tasya jīvitam
english: But the man who, having eaten what is wholesome, then out of greed eats other food, heedless of the consequence, finds in that the end of his life.

sanskrit: daivaṃ puruṣakāraś ca sthitāv anyonyasaṃśrayāt udāttānāṃ karma tantraṃ daivaṃ klībā upāsate
english: Destiny and human effort both stand by mutual support; for the high-minded, action is the rule; only the feeble rely upon destiny alone.

sanskrit: karma cātmahitaṃ kāryaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ vā yadi vā mṛdu grasyate 'karmaśīlas tu sadānarthair akiṃcanaḥ
english: One should perform the act conducive to one's good, whether harsh or gentle; but the man of idle habit, possessing nothing, is forever devoured by misfortunes.

sanskrit: tasmāt saṃśayite 'py arthe kārya eva parākramaḥ sarvasvam api saṃtyajya kāryam ātmahitaṃ naraiḥ
english: Therefore, even where the outcome is in doubt, one must still exert oneself; men should accomplish what serves their own good, even at the cost of all they have.

sanskrit: vidyā śauryaṃ ca dākṣyaṃ ca balaṃ dhairyaṃ ca pañcamam mitrāṇi sahajāny āhur vartayantīha yair budhāḥ
english: Learning, valor, skill, strength, and steadfastness as the fifth: these the wise call one's innate friends, by which they make their way in the world.

sanskrit: niveśanaṃ ca kupyaṃ ca kṣetraṃ bhāryā suhṛjjanaḥ etāny upacitāny āhuḥ sarvatra labhate pumān
english: A dwelling, household goods, a field, a wife, and friendly folk: these they call one's acquired possessions, which a man may gain anywhere.

sanskrit: sarvatra ramate prājñaḥ sarvatra ca virocate na vibhīṣayate kaṃ cid bhīṣito na bibheti ca
english: The wise man finds delight everywhere and shines everywhere; he frightens no one, and when threatened himself, he does not fear.

sanskrit: nityaṃ buddhimato hy arthaḥ svalpako 'pi vivardhate dākṣyeṇa kurute karma saṃyamāt pratitiṣṭhati
english: For the intelligent man, wealth, however small, ever increases; through skill he accomplishes his work, and through self-restraint he stands secure.

sanskrit: gṛhasnehāvabaddhānāṃ narāṇām alpamedhasām kustrī khādati māṃsāni māghamā segavām iva
english: Of men of little understanding, bound fast by attachment to home, an evil wife devours the very flesh, as a she-tiger devours cattle.

sanskrit: gṛhaṃ kṣetrāṇi mitrāṇi svadeśa iti cāpare ity evam avasīdanti narā buddhiviparyaye
english: "My home, my fields, my friends, my own land": so cling some, and thus, in their perversity of mind, men sink to ruin.

sanskrit: utpatet sarujād deśād vyādhidurbhikṣapīḍitāt anyatra vastuṃ gacched vā vased vā nityamānitaḥ
english: From a land sick with calamity, oppressed by disease and famine, one should fly away to dwell elsewhere, or settle where one is ever held in honor.

sanskrit: tasmād anyatra yāsyāmi vastuṃ nāham ihotsahe kṛtam etad anāhāryaṃ tava putreṇa pārthiva
english: Therefore I shall go elsewhere to dwell; I cannot bring myself to stay here. What your son has done is past all undoing, O king.

sanskrit: kubhāryāṃ ca kuputraṃ ca kurājānaṃ kusauhṛdam kusaṃbandhaṃ kudeśaṃ ca dūrataḥ parivarjayet
english: A bad wife, a bad son, a bad king, a bad friendship, a bad alliance, and a bad country: all these one should shun from afar.

sanskrit: kumitre nāsti viśvāsaḥ kubhāryāyāṃ kuto ratiḥ kurājye nirvṛtir nāsti kudeśe na prajīvyate
english: In a bad friend there is no trust; in a bad wife, where is delight? In a bad realm there is no peace; in a bad country one cannot make a living.

sanskrit: kumitre saṃgataṃ nāsti nityam asthirasauhṛde avamānaḥ kusaṃbandhe bhavaty arthaviparyaye
english: With a bad friend, whose goodwill is ever unsteady, there is no true fellowship; in a bad alliance there comes only dishonor, and the ruin of one's interests.

sanskrit: sā bhāryā yā priyaṃ brūte sa putro yatra nirvṛtiḥ tan mitraṃ yatra viśvāsaḥ sa deśo yatra jīvyate
english: She is a wife who speaks what is dear; he is a son in whom there is contentment; that is a friend in whom there is trust; that is a country where one can live.

sanskrit: yatra nāsti balātkāraḥ sa rājā tīvraśāsanaḥ na caiva hy abhisaṃbandho daridraṃ yo bubhūṣati
english: He is a king of firm rule under whom there is no oppression; nor is that a true kinship which wishes to keep a man in poverty.

sanskrit: bhāryā deśo 'tha mitrāṇi putrasaṃbandhibāndhavāḥ etat sarvaṃ guṇavati dharmanetre mahīpatau
english: Wife, country, friends, sons, kinsmen, and relations: all of this thrives under a virtuous king whose guide is dharma.

sanskrit: adharmajñasya vilayaṃ prajā gacchanty anigrahāt rājā mūlaṃ trivargasya apramatto 'nupālayan
english: Under one ignorant of dharma, the subjects go to their dissolution for want of restraint; the king is the root of the threefold aim, when he guards it with unflagging care.

sanskrit: baliṣaḍbhāgam uddhṛtya baliṃ tam upayojayet na rakṣati prajāḥ samyag yaḥ sa pārthivataskaraḥ
english: Having levied a sixth part as tribute, he should employ that tribute well; the king who does not rightly protect his subjects is but a royal thief.

sanskrit: dattvābhayaṃ yaḥ svayam eva rājā; na tat pramāṇaṃ kurute yathāvat sa sarvalokād upalabhya pāpam; adharmabuddhir nirayaṃ prayāti
english: The king who, having himself granted safety, does not duly hold to that pledge, takes upon himself the sin of all the world, and, his mind set on unrighteousness, goes down to hell.

sanskrit: dattvābhayaṃ yaḥ sma rājā pramāṇaṃ kurute sadā sa sarvasukhakṛj jñeyaḥ prajā dharmeṇa pālayan
english: But the king who, having granted safety, ever holds firm to his pledge is to be known as the maker of all happiness, guarding his subjects by dharma.

sanskrit: pitā mātā gurur goptā vahnir vaiśravaṇo yamaḥ sapta rājño guṇān etān manur āha prajāpatiḥ
english: Father, mother, teacher, protector, Fire, Vaiśravaṇa, and Yama: these seven qualities of a king did Manu, the lord of creatures, proclaim.

sanskrit: pitā hi rājā rāṣṭrasya prajānāṃ yo 'nukampakaḥ tasmin mithyāpraṇīte hi tiryag gacchati mānavaḥ
english: The king is a father to the kingdom, one who has compassion for his subjects; but when he is led astray, a man goes astray as well.

sanskrit: saṃbhāvayati māteva dīnam abhyavapadyate dahaty agnir ivāniṣṭān yamayan bhavate yamaḥ
english: Like a mother he cherishes them, and succors the helpless; like fire he burns the wicked, and in restraining men he becomes a very Yama.

sanskrit: iṣṭeṣu visṛjaty arthān kubera iva kāmadaḥ gurur dharmopadeśena goptā ca paripālanāt
english: Upon the deserving he lavishes wealth, a granter of wishes like Kubera; he is a teacher through his instruction in dharma, and a protector through his guarding care.

sanskrit: yas tu rañjayate rājā paurajānapadān guṇaiḥ na tasya bhraśyate rājyaṃ guṇadharmānupālanāt
english: The king who gladdens by his virtues the people of the city and the countryside does not lose his realm, for he upholds both virtue and dharma.

sanskrit: svayaṃ samupajānan hi paurajānapadakriyāḥ sa sukhaṃ modate bhūpa iha loke paratra ca
english: For the lord of earth who himself looks well into the affairs of city and countryside rejoices in happiness, in this world and the next.

sanskrit: nityodvignāḥ prajā yasya karabhāraprapīḍitāḥ anarthair vipralupyante sa gacchati parābhavam
english: That king whose subjects, ever anxious, are crushed by the burden of taxes and are stripped bare by calamities, goes to his downfall.

sanskrit: prajā yasya vivardhante sarasīva mahotpalam sa sarvayajñaphalabhāg rājā loke mahīyate
english: But that king under whom the subjects flourish, like the great lotus in a lake, shares in the fruit of every sacrifice and is honored in the world.

sanskrit: balinā vigraho rājan na kathaṃ cit praśasyate balinā vigṛhītasya kuto rājyaṃ kutaḥ sukham
english: War with one stronger than oneself, O king, is in no way to be commended; for one at strife with a stronger foe, where is the kingdom, and where the happiness?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca saivam uktvā śakunikā brahmadattaṃ narādhipam rājānaṃ samanujñāpya jagāmāthepsitāṃ diśam
english: Bhīṣma said: Having thus spoken, the bird, taking leave of King Brahmadatta, the ruler of men, departed to the quarter she desired.

sanskrit: etat te brahmadattasya pūjanyā saha bhāṣitam mayoktaṃ bharataśreṣṭha kim anyac chrotum icchasi
english: This converse of Brahmadatta with Pūjanī I have now recounted to you, O best of the Bhāratas. What else do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yugakṣayāt parikṣīṇe dharme loke ca bhārata dasyubhiḥ pīḍyamāne ca kathaṃ stheyaṃ pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When, through the waning of the age, dharma has dwindled away and the world too, O Bhārata, is oppressed by bandits, how should one conduct oneself, O grandsire?
